category_scope: Chef's knife and adjacent kitchen cutlery. Excludes hunting, folding/pocket, and tactical knife use cases at topic-ID resolution per v1.2 §4.

lineage_extension.note: Discourse-Language Knives — v0.16 carries forward the substrate under v1.2 construct-validity panel

brand_age_convention.rule_definition: Brand age is measured from the date the brand mark was publicly introduced to the kitchen-knives market, NOT from parent-enterprise founding or traditional-craft lineage. Convention chosen for consistency across panel; resolves the parent-company / acquired-brand / craft-tradition confound that occurs in knives but did not occur in v0.14/v0.15 tea (where company = brand mark coincidence held).

applied_cases.shun: Kai Group parent founded 1908; Shun brand mark publicly introduced c. 2002 (Kai USA Ltd.). Coded 2002.
applied_cases.miyabi: Zwilling J.A. Henckels parent founded 1731; Miyabi brand mark introduced 2004. Coded 2004.
applied_cases.yoshihiro: Sakai blacksmith tradition spans multiple generations; Yoshihiro Cutlery modern brand-bearing enterprise registered 1996. Coded 1996.
applied_cases.made_in: Made In brand mark introduced 2017 (cookware); cutlery line launched 2019 as product extension. Brand-mark date used. Coded 2017.
applied_cases.shibazi: '十八子' craft tradition older; Yangjiang Shibazi modern brand-bearing enterprise founded 1983. Coded 1983.

brand_age_convention.rule_override: If Pablo's v0.14/v0.15 convention differs, this file should be re-emitted with the corrected rule. The MSI WP cross-citation discussion should note any cross-phase convention divergence explicitly.

tier_definitions.premium: Hand-forged or artisan-scale production; typical chef knife > USD 250; restaurant high-end and connoisseur market
tier_definitions.professional: Industrial-scale production with restaurant-grade reputation; typical chef knife USD 100–250; mainstream professional adoption
tier_definitions.accessible: Industrial-scale production targeted at serious home cooks; typical chef knife USD 40–100
tier_definitions.value: Mass-market or regional-market production; typical chef knife < USD 40

primary.rationale: Chef-knife sub-category (Swiss Classic / Fibrox line) is the restaurant-industry workhorse with high global volume, broad search-interest base, and low brand-age signal interference. Swiss-Army-knife adjacency is a topic-ID concern (resolved at v1.2 §4 5-stage) rather than a search-interest stability concern.
